THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE S.K. SAHOO  THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE CHITTARANJAN DASH  ORDER Order No. 01.10.2024 01.
This matter is taken up through Hybrid arrangement (video conferencing/physical mode).
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned counsel for the State.

The petitioner has filed this writ petition with a prayer to direct the opposite parties to pay compensation and solatium for acquisition of the land with fruit bearing trees as per the present market value with interest @ 12% and solatium 100% for acquisition of the land of the petitioner.

Mr. Amitav Das, learned counsel for the opposite parties drew the attention of this Court to the letter dated 01.09.2023 issued by the Project Director, National Highway Authority of India,
opposite party no.1, which indicates that liberty was granted to the petitioner to file objection under section 3C of the N.H. Act, 1956 along with documents establishing his right, title and interest over the land as per law.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner admittedly has not filed any objection along with documents as per the letter dated 01.09.2023.

He drew the attention of this Court to Annexure-4 and Annexure-5 and submitted that the Land Acquisition Officer and Competent Authority, N.H. 215 Project, Keonjhar has mentioned therein the extent of land previously acquired Shiba Prasad Palei vs National Highway .... sentences.text:
It is stated that even though that land has been acquired subsequently,
but no compensation amount has been paid.

Considering the submissions made by the learned counsel for the respective parties, we dispose of the writ petition granting liberty to the petitioner to file his objection along with documents as mentioned in the letter dated 01.09.2023 before the opposite party no.2 within a period one month from today.

On receipt of such objection and documents, the opposite party no.2 shall take a decision thereon within a period of four weeks from the date of filing of such objection in accordance with law after giving opportunity of personal hearing to the petitioner, if required and decision taken thereon shall be communicated to the petitioner within a period of fifteen days from the date of taking such decision.
Issue urgent certified copy as per rules.
( S.K. Sahoo) Judge (Chittaranjan Dash) Judge M.K.Rout Shiba Prasad Palei vs National Highway .... Opp.
